title: International Classification of Sleep Disorders, Third Edition
authority: classification source subject to ICSD-3-TR updates
apaReference: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
revisionReference: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
revisionPolicy: ICSD-3-TR nomenclature and criteria changes override older ICSD-3 wording when a conflict exists.
copyrightBoundary: Glossary term names are inventoried. Learner definitions and memory clues are original Sleep Pathways Guild summaries rather than reproduced ICSD glossary prose.

items.definition: A method that uses a motion-sensing device, often worn on the wrist, to estimate patterns of sleep and wake across time.
items.memoryClue: Actigraphy estimates sleep-wake patterns from movement.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Inadequate ventilation of the gas-exchanging portions of the lungs relative to carbon dioxide production, leading to elevated arterial CO2.
items.memoryClue: Too little alveolar ventilation raises PaCO2.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The arterial CO2 level below which respiratory drive can fall enough for central apnea to occur during NREM sleep.
items.memoryClue: Below the CO2 threshold, central breathing pauses can appear.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: An irregular breathing pattern with variable tidal volumes and respiratory rates, classically associated with opioid effects.
items.memoryClue: Ataxic means irregular in depth and timing.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A sudden increase in autonomic activity during sleep, such as increased sympathetic tone, heart rate, or blood pressure.
items.memoryClue: Autonomic arousal may occur without an obvious cortical EEG arousal.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Internal circadian phases that favor wakefulness during the biological day and sleep during the biological night.
items.memoryClue: Biological time is set by the circadian system, not simply the clock.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Brief episodes of sudden muscle weakness with consciousness preserved, typically triggered by strong emotion.
items.memoryClue: Emotion-triggered weakness with awareness preserved.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The responsiveness of respiratory control systems to changes in carbon dioxide and oxygen.
items.memoryClue: Chemoreceptors adjust ventilation when CO2 or O2 changes.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A person’s preferred timing for sleep, waking, and daily activity, often described along a morningness-eveningness spectrum.
items.memoryClue: Chronotype = preferred timing.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A mismatch between a person’s internal circadian timing and the timing of sleep, wake, or required activities.
items.memoryClue: The body clock and the schedule are out of sync.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The duration of one full cycle of an internal circadian rhythm.
items.memoryClue: Tau is the length of one circadian cycle.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The timing of a specific point within a circadian cycle, such as a peak, trough, onset, or offset.
items.memoryClue: Phase tells where you are in the circadian cycle.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: An internally generated biological rhythm with a period close to 24 hours.
items.memoryClue: Circadian rhythms are near-24-hour clock-driven cycles.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Insomnia that occurs alongside another condition but may have mechanisms and treatment needs that are partly independent.
items.memoryClue: Coexisting does not necessarily mean caused entirely by the other disorder.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Learned wakefulness or tension triggered by repeated association of the sleep environment with unsuccessful attempts to sleep.
items.memoryClue: The bed can become a cue for wakefulness.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A brief shift toward faster EEG activity indicating activation of the cerebral cortex during sleep.
items.memoryClue: Cortical arousal is identified in EEG.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A repeating NREM EEG pattern of transient activation phases alternating with background phases and associated with sleep instability.
items.memoryClue: CAP reflects unstable NREM sleep.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The circadian phase marker defined by the evening rise of melatonin measured under dim-light conditions.
items.memoryClue: DLMO is a clock marker measured in dim light.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Relating to dopamine or to neural systems that use dopamine as a neurotransmitter.
items.memoryClue: Dopaminergic = dopamine-related.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Involuntary sustained or intermittent muscle contractions that produce abnormal movements or postures.
items.memoryClue: Dystonia causes abnormal postures or repetitive movements.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Waking earlier than desired with reduced total sleep time and inability to maintain the intended sleep period.
items.memoryClue: Sleep ends too early.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: A recording of electrical activity generated by muscles, commonly obtained from surface electrodes during sleep testing.
items.memoryClue: EMG records muscle electrical activity.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The state or process in which an internal circadian rhythm becomes synchronized to an external time cue or environmental cycle.
items.memoryClue: Entrainment locks the body clock to a time cue.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Reduced energy or capacity for activity that is distinct from the physiologic tendency to fall asleep.
items.memoryClue: Fatigue is low energy; sleepiness is propensity to sleep.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: The process by which the body regulates internal conditions to maintain physiologic balance.
items.memoryClue: Homeostasis keeps internal conditions stable.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: An abnormally elevated arterial carbon dioxide level.
items.memoryClue: Hypercapnia = high PaCO2.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.

items.definition: Excessive sleepiness occurring during the usual waking period.
items.memoryClue: Hypersomnolence describes excessive daytime sleepiness.
references: American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2014). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
American Academy of Sleep Medicine. (2023). International classification of sleep disorders (3rd ed., text rev.). American Academy of Sleep Medicine.
